originalTitle: Small investors became a major stock market force. Now, they risk getting pushed back into the dark
summary: Retail investors' access to information could take a hit at a time when they are more important than ever in financial markets.
content:
After years of standing in the sun, retail investors could have a dark cloud forming over their heads.

Technological advancements helped level the playing field for Main Street and Wall Street investors over decades. Following the Covid trading boom and a banner performance in 2025 , individual investors became a mainstay of today's markets and shook off their "dumb money" stigma.

But advocates for small investors now warn that efforts to change corporate earnings , Federal Reserve communication and social media access could undo a sizable chunk of that progress. These shifts would disadvantage retail investors at a time when they are a more powerful force than ever in financial markets.

"We are almost taking steps backwards," said Hardika Singh, economic strategist at asset manager Fundstrat. "It's almost making me wonder: Are we sort of entering this information blackout age for a very important subset of the stock market?"

There's three key storylines market participants are tracking that could hurt the retail crowd:

The Securities and Exchange Commission in May backed President Donald Trump 's proposal for public companies to report earnings biannually instead of quarterly. SEC Chairman Paul Atkins said in a statement that the organization's "rigid" rules have stopped companies from finding a reporting cadence that "best serves their business needs."

Investors acknowledge that required quarterly reports can strain corporate resources and keep firms from going public . But having less of these audited releases could result in an information vacuum for retail investors, according to Siebert Financial's Mark Malek. More unofficial content or misinformation could arise as a result, he said.

Quarterly earnings reports are "the gold standard," said Malek, the firm's investing chief. "Taking that away is definitely disadvantaging the retail investor."

In a poll on retail investing platform Moomoo, U.S. CEO Neil McDonald found that most users disliked the prospect of switching to a twice-yearly reporting cycle. If retail investors have less-frequent insight into financial performance, McDonald said that they would likely become more hesitant to invest in small-cap, high-growth companies.

McDonald remembers working at Goldman Sachs in the 1980s when analysts would jet off to a company's headquarters to collect earnings reports. The analyst would dictate the results by phone, allowing the bank to quickly alert its institutional clients. A retail investor likely wouldn't know how the company performed until the newspaper arrived a day later, he said.

Wall Street has a history of using unconventional mechanisms when official information is difficult to find. Before the SEC mandated quarterly earnings in 1970, firms tracked data like weekly rail car loadings for clues on the direction of economic activity. When China was a black box for American investors, traders followed coal shipments to the country as a leading indicator for production.

If there are fewer earnings reports, institutional investors will be able to lean on their teams of analysts, who often have direct access to a company's C-suite. Small-scale investors, on the other hand, typically only hear directly from these executives by listening into earnings calls or tracking their public appearances.

"The chief financial officer is not likely going to take a call from Joe Blow," said Sam Stovall, chief investment strategist at CFRA Research, whose firm advertises services for both big and small investors. "But they would take a call from a very high-profile institutional investor."

New Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh has cut down the central bank's policy meeting statement and removed forward guidance . Warsh, who has promised sweeping changes in how the Fed communicates, also floated the idea of having fewer of these gatherings.

Hearing less from the Fed can make it harder for retail to set expectations for the economy and monetary policy, which can be important factors when deciding overall portfolio allocation. Additionally, small investors have a penchant for technology stocks whose growth outlooks are dependent in part on borrowing costs determined by the Fed.

Markets have already had less clear of a consensus heading into the first two Fed meetings under Warsh when compared against recent history. With less policy hints from the Fed, investors anticipate more volatility after policy decisions are announced.

Wall Street firms have built out artificial intelligence-powered tools to keep a handle on the Fed in the lower-communication environment. Several of these institutions have economists — and, in many cases, Fed alumni — on staff to predict what the central bank's next move could mean for markets.

If the macroeconomic picture becomes harder to gauge, CFRA's Stovall said small investors may look to financial advisors for help.

Truth Media & Technology Group 's launch of Truth API — a paid data service providing faster access to Truth Social posts — heightened the concern of retail investors having the cards stacked against them.

Trump Media did not respond to CNBC's questions about exact details around the cost of the offering or how early of access it offers. But interim CEO Kevin McGurn told analysts this week that it has inked more than 10 customer agreements for the API in a price range of between $60,000 and $100,000 per month. McGurn described the service as providing "fractionally faster" access.

Multiple of the S&P 500 's best and worst days during Trump's second term have been driven by posts he made on Truth Social , a Fundstrat data analysis found.

"He has the market in the palm of his hands," said Fundstrat's Singh. "Never before in history has a president exerted this level of control via social media."

chineseTitle: 小投资者成为股市的主要力量。现在，他们面临着被推回黑暗的风险
chineseSummary: 当散户投资者在金融市场上比以往任何时候都更加重要时，他们获取信息的能力可能会受到打击。
chineseContent:
经过多年站在阳光下，散户投资者的头顶可能会形成乌云。

几十年来，技术进步帮助大街和华尔街投资者创造了公平的竞争环境。继新冠疫情带来的交易热潮和 2025 年的出色表现之后，个人投资者成为当今市场的中流砥柱，摆脱了“傻钱”的污名。

但小投资者的倡导者现在警告说，改变企业盈利、美联储沟通和社交媒体访问的努力可能会抵消很大一部分进展。这些转变将使散户投资者处于不利地位，因为散户投资者在金融市场上的力量比以往任何时候都更加强大。

资产管理公司 Fundstrat 的经济策略师哈迪卡·辛格 (Hardika Singh) 表示：“我们几乎在倒退。” “这几乎让我想知道：对于股票市场的一个非常重要的子集来说，我们是否正在进入这个信息封锁时代？”

市场参与者正在追踪的三个关键故事情节可能会伤害散户：

美国证券交易委员会五月支持唐纳德·特朗普总统关于上市公司每半年而不是每季度报告收益的提议。美国证券交易委员会主席保罗·阿特金斯在一份声明中表示，该组织的“严格”规则阻止了公司找到“最能满足其业务需求”的报告节奏。

投资者承认，所要求的季度报告可能会导致公司资源紧张，并阻碍公司上市。但 Siebert Financial 的马克·马利克 (Mark Malek) 表示，减少这些经过审计的发布可能会导致散户投资者出现信息真空。他说，结果可能会出现更多非官方内容或错误信息。

该公司投资主管马利克表示，季度收益报告是“黄金标准”。 “取消这一点肯定会让散户投资者处于不利地位。”

在零售投资平台 Moomoo 的一项民意调查中，美国首席执行官尼尔·麦克唐纳 (Neil McDonald) 发现，大多数用户不喜欢改用每年两次的报告周期。麦克唐纳表示，如果散户投资者不太频繁地了解财务业绩，他们可能会在投资小盘股、高增长公司时变得更加犹豫。

McDonald 记得 20 世纪 80 年代在高盛工作，当时分析师会飞往公司总部收集收益报告。分析师将通过电话说出结果，从而使银行能够快速提醒其机构客户。他说，散户投资者可能直到一天后报纸到达才知道该公司的表现如何。

当官方信息难以找到时，华尔街就有使用非常规机制的历史。 1970 年，在 SEC 强制公布季度收益之前，企业会追踪每周火车车厢装载量等数据，以寻找有关经济活动方向的线索。当中国对美国投资者来说是一个黑匣子时，交易员们将煤炭运往该国的情况作为生产的领先指标。

如果收益报告较少，机构投资者将能够依靠他们的分析师团队，这些分析师通常可以直接接触公司的最高管理层。另一方面，小规模投资者通常只能通过听取财报电话会议或跟踪他们的公开露面来直接听取这些高管的意见。

CFRA Research 的首席投资策略师萨姆·斯托瓦尔 (Sam Stovall) 表示：“首席财务官不太可能接乔·布洛 (Joe Blow) 的电话。”CFRA Research 的公司为大型和小型投资者提供服务广告。 “但他们会接到一位非常知名的机构投资者的电话。”

新任美联储主席凯文·沃什削减了央行政策会议声明并取消了前瞻性指引。沃什承诺对美联储的沟通方式进行彻底改变，他还提出了减少此类聚会的想法。

减少美联储的消息可能会让零售业更难设定对经济和货币政策的预期，而这可能是决定整体投资组合配置的重要因素。此外，小投资者偏爱科技股，其增长前景部分取决于美联储确定的借贷成本。

与最近的历史相比，在沃什领导下的前两次美联储会议上，市场已经不太明确达成共识。由于美联储的政策暗示较少，投资者预计政策决定公布后波动将会更大。

华尔街公司已经开发出了人工智能驱动的工具，以便在沟通不畅的环境中控制美联储。其中一些机构的工作人员中有经济学家——在很多情况下还有美联储校友——来预测央行的下一步行动可能对市场意味着什么。

CFRA 的斯托瓦尔表示，如果宏观经济形势变得更难以衡量，小投资者可能会向财务顾问寻求帮助。

Truth Media & Technology Group 推出的 Truth API（一种付费数据服务，可以更快地访问 Truth Social 帖子）加剧了散户投资者对自己不利的担忧。

特朗普媒体没有回应 CNBC 提出的有关该产品的成本或提供多早访问的具体细节的问题。但临时首席执行官 Kevin McGurn 本周告诉分析师，该公司已签署了 10 多项 API 客户协议，价格范围为每月 60,000 美元至 100,000 美元。麦格恩将该服务描述为提供“稍微更快”的访问。

Fundstrat 数据分析发现，特朗普第二个任期内，标普 500 指数表现最好和最差的日子中有多个是由他在 Truth Social 上发表的帖子推动的。

Fundstrat 的辛格表示：“市场掌握在他的手中。” “历史上从未有一位总统通过社交媒体施加过如此程度的控制。”

一些投资者告诉 CNBC，特朗普有动力发布更多影响市场的 Truth Social 帖子，以激发人们对 API 的兴趣。特朗普家族是特朗普媒体的最大股东，该公司回购
